 AMD Stock Could Surprise on the Upside, but One Number Matters Most
 AMD has surged over 150% this year and landed massive GPU deals with OpenAI and Anthropic, yet one metric keeps our rating stuck at hold. Here is the number that could finally change that.
 By Vandita Jadeja 
 Published October 29, 2026, 9:33am ET · 3 min read 
 Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja .
 𝕏 
 f 
 ⧉ 
 Quick Read
 AMD earns a HOLD rating with a $543 price target, as today's 3% gain pushed shares just past fair value.
 Anthropic plans to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 GPUs in Helios racks, with Lisa Su saying demand is "tracking ahead of our initial forecast."
 NVIDIA earns a 60% operating margin against AMD's 11%, yet both trade at roughly 43 times earnings.

 The 24/7 Wall St. price target for AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD | AMD Price Prediction ) is $542.87 over the next 12 months. Shares trade at $549.58 this morning, so the target implies -1.2% downside. We rate AMD a hold with high confidence.

 The model ran against the close of $531.29, where it showed 2.18% upside. This morning’s 3.44% gain raised shares just past fair value.
 Data Center revenue, the key driver, reached $6.72B last quarter, 58% of sales , with the division expected to “more than double year-over-year in 2027.”
 Why We Could Be Wrong
 AMD trades slightly above our target, and the upside drivers are real. Anthropic plans to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 GPUs in Helios racks, and Lisa Su said Helios demand is “tracking ahead of our initial forecast.” Our target is one point among many, and the bull case below shows how AMD could beat it.
 A 156% Rally Meets an October Pullback
 AMD is up 156.62% year to date, but shares fell 12.85% over the past month before rising 2.14% this week. The stock trades 16.5% below its 52-week high of $658.52 and well above its low of $188.22.
 In Q2, revenue grew 50.1% to $11.54B, beating the $11.31B estimate. EPS came in at $1.66, ahead of the $1.61 consensus. Q3 guidance calls for roughly $13B.
 The latest news is a large stock offering from Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) to fund AI expansion. MarketWatch reports that AMD, NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) and Broadcom ( NASDAQ:AVGO ) could buy shares in it (MarketWatch).
 Why Bulls See $688 Ahead
 The bull case reaches $688.72 . Management expects server revenue to grow more than 80% in the second half of 2026 and more than 70% in 2027. AMD also expects EPS to beat its $20 long-term target by a wide margin.
 The OpenAI (6 GW) and Meta (up to 6 GW) deals give that plan real backing. Wall Street agrees: 5 Strong Buy ratings, 40 Buys, 11 Holds and no Sells , with a consensus target of $637.61.
 What Could Pull AMD Toward $430
 The bear case is $430.83. AMD trades at 200 times trailing earnings, and Gaming revenue fell 31%. Export controls previously forced an $800M MI308 inventory charge, and server CPU supply remains tight. Free cash flow dropped 9.89% to $1.56B.
 Bulls would answer that inventory of about $8.5 billion is being built ahead of the Helios ramp. They would also point to the non-GAAP operating margin, which expanded to 27% from 12%.
 AMD Trades at NVIDIA’s Multiple With Room to Catch Up
 NVIDIA is AMD’s direct competition in AI GPUs. It trades at 43 times trailing earnings, roughly AMD’s 43 forward multiple, while earning a 60% operating margin against AMD’s 10.66%.
 Broadcom competes for the same hyperscaler AI budgets with custom accelerators. Its AI semiconductor revenue rose 221% to $16.70 billion. Both peers are growing AI revenue faster on higher margins, which makes our target look reasonable.

 Data Center Proof Could Shift Our HOLD Rating
 The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $542.87 supports a hold at 90% confidence. Valuation is the deciding factor : the stock already prices in much of the Helios ramp.
 Our rating would turn more positive if Q3 Data Center results show Helios shipments speeding up into Q4. Our view would turn more cautious if supply limits or export rules slow that ramp. For now, AMD looks fairly valued.
